blinding_guess.why: B ships a test suite and keeps policy.json as the single source of truth, which might suggest a spec-driven process, but this signal is weak.

notes: Both implementations pass every core probe: per-class rules, case-insensitive forbidden list, all failures reported, Shannon entropy (identical formula), policy-satisfying generation with the secrets module, and validation errors without tracebacks. A's main defect is that check/generate do not read policy.json unless -p is given, so a user's policy file is silently ignored. A also adds unrequested extras (substring matching of common passwords, pool entropy, --json), which are harmless. Bandit reported no findings for either side. B's tests pass when run with PYTHONPATH=. (7/7); A has no tests.
